chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Harun ibn Muslim, from Mas'ada ibn Sadaqa, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
The lowering (of the female child's genitals) is a noble deed, and it is not from the Sunnah, nor is it anything obligatory, and which thing is more preferable than the noble deed?

key_terms.خَفْضُ الْجَارِيَةِ: Lowering/cutting of the female child's genitals
key_terms.مَكْرُمَةٌ: A noble deed or act of generosity

ai.seo_question: Is female circumcision considered obligatory or part of the Sunnah in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In this narration from al-Kafi, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) clarifies the juridical status of female circumcision (khafd al-jariya), distinguishing it from obligatory duties (wajib) and established Prophetic Sunnah, thereby classifying it as a virtuous custom (makrumah). This distinction reflects the Shia scholarly view that while the practice is recommended for hygiene or modesty, it is not a mandatory pillar of faith. The rhetorical emphasis on 'nobility' underscores its value as a praiseworthy act of care rather than a strict religious obligation.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, form his father, from Haroun Bin Muslim, from Mas’ada Bin Sadaqa, 
Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> has said:
‘Cutting the (genitals) of the girls is a noble deed, and it is not from the Sunnah, nor anything Obligatory, and which thing is more preferable to the noble deed?’
en.sarwar: 3. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from Harun ibn Muslim from Mas’adah ibn Sadaqah who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘
Reducing for girls is a noble trait but it is not of the Sunnah or obligatory; however, a noble trait is a very preferred matter.’”
